label: copy phase: input n/p/j/1/f/0 while outputting 1 or n (token preceding a 1)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.03% of steps). 99.6% of activation mass is in the copy phase (t > L), at recall_idx >= 2, never on original tokens or the delimiter. It fires when the input token is one of n, p, j, 1, f, 0 (also y, k more weakly) and the token being output is the digit 1 (55% of mass, 33x lift) or n. Typical case: the copy input just before a 1 in the original string, e.g. ...n [p] 1... Top activations come from n/1/j clusters such as 0 n [j] [n] 1. Activation is stronger with longer L and later recall positions, and weaker at the last output. It does not fire on most letters as input (a, m, w, z are near zero). Precision is low (~5%): most steps that match the input/output token pair do not activate, so the feature evidently depends on further hidden-state context that this predicate does not capture.
